s2.p1: Mexico has a **WDSF member federation**, and its couples dance on the WDSF circuit, from Cali 2016 to Cali 2026, in Standard and Latin.
s2.p2: Its people’s ballroom is the **salón de baile**. Mexico City’s Salón Los Ángeles has hosted danzón, mambo and salsa with live bands since ==1937==.

s3.p: performed the **Jarabe Tapatío** in Guadalajara in 2019, to live mariachi. A Guinness World Record, nearly double the 457 of 2011.

s4.p1: Choreographer **Amalia Hernández** started out with just eight dancers. In **1959**, a presidential decree created the Ballet Folklórico.
s4.p2: It has toured ==300+ cities in 60 countries==, and still dances at Mexico City’s **Palacio de Bellas Artes**.

s5.name: VOLADORES
s5.p: Four men leap from a pole **18 to 40 metres** high, tied by ropes, and spin to the ground. A fifth plays flute and drum on the top.

s5.name: PARACHICOS
s5.p: Dancers in **carved wooden masks**, serapes and ribbons shake maracas through the streets, from 4 to 23 January, as an offering to three saints.

s6.p: Danzón was born in 19th-century Cuba, where it is now kept alive by older fans. Mexico kept dancing: in Veracruz, couples met on the main square **four times a week**.

s7.p: Mexico City declares danzón **Intangible Cultural Heritage**. Every week it fills La Ciudadela and the Monumento a la Revolución.
s7.p2: **600** people dance huapango at once in this Pueblo Mágico: a new Guinness World Record.
